ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Oxygen is carried in the blood by the respiratory pigment hemoglobin, which can combine loosely with four oxygen molecules, forming the molecule oxyhemoglobin. To function properly, hemoglobin must bind to oxygen in the lungs and drop it off at body cells. The more easily the hemoglobin binds to oxygen in the lungs, the more difficult the oxygen is to unload at the body cells. Here is a graph showing two different saturation-dissociation curves for one type of hemoglobin at two different pH levels.

Based on your knowledge of biology and the information in this graph, which statement about the hemoglobin curves is correct?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a graph of hemoglobin oxygen saturation changing with PO2, with the vertical axis as Hb's O2 saturation and the horizontal axis as PO2. There are two curves in the figure: the curve labeled pH 7.4 is positioned more to the left and higher; the curve labeled pH 7.2 is positioned more to the right and lower. Reasoning: An acidic environment means a lower pH, so one should look at the pH 7.2 curve. Under the same body-cell PO2 condition, the oxygen saturation of the pH 7.2 curve is lower than that of the pH 7.4 curve. Lower oxygen saturation indicates that hemoglobin binds less oxygen, that is, more oxygen is released or unloaded. Therefore, an acidic environment makes hemoglobin more easily release oxygen at body cells.
